`+` with a string operand concatenates: `1 + '1'` becomes `'11'`. Then `-` always forces numeric coercion: `'11' - 1` is `10`.

exercises.prompt: This function is meant to check whether `s` is a palindrome, but `is_palindrome("abba")` incorrectly returns `False`. What's the bug?
choices: `s[-i]` should be `s[-i - 1]`, since `s[-0]` is the same element as `s[0]`
The comparison should use `==` instead of `!=`
Strings can't be indexed with negative numbers in Python
exercises.answer: `s[-i]` should be `s[-i - 1]`, since `s[-0]` is the same element as `s[0]`
exercises.explanation: `-i` and `i` refer to the *same* character when `i` is 0 (both mean index 0), so the intended "from the end" index needs `-i - 1`, e.g. `s[-1]` for the last character.

exercises.prompt: This function is meant to process every item and only log `'done'` after all of them finish. It doesn't work as intended. What's the bug?
choices: `Array.prototype.forEach` doesn't wait for the async callbacks — `'done'` logs before any `process(item)` call resolves
`async` callbacks aren't allowed as arguments to `forEach`, so this throws an error
`await` can't be used inside an arrow function
`items` needs to be awaited before calling `forEach` on it
exercises.answer: `Array.prototype.forEach` doesn't wait for the async callbacks — `'done'` logs before any `process(item)` call resolves
exercises.explanation: `forEach` ignores the promises returned by its callback and never awaits them; use a `for...of` loop with `await`, or `Promise.all` with `map`, to actually wait for every item.

exercises.prompt: What is the time complexity of `has_unique_chars` as a function of `n = len(s)`, in the worst case?
exercises.explanation: The nested loop compares every pair of characters, giving roughly $n^2/2$ comparisons in the worst case (no matches found) — O(n^2).
